title: Agent Token Spend by Consumer
dataSources: Trace and agent span metadata key `consumer`, and per-trace cost and token counts
description: Shows who is spending tokens on an agent by filtering the Splunk Agent Observability trace table on a `consumer` metadata key set on the trace and on the agent spans.
value: Shared agents need chargeback or at least a conversation with the heaviest users. A consumer key on every trace makes that a filter rather than a project.
implementation: Set `metadata={"consumer": user_id}` on `start_trace` and on the agent spans. Filter the trace table by `consumer` and sort by cost or tokens. Use an internal user or team id, not raw PII.
visualization: Trace table filtered by consumer, sorted by cost; token totals per consumer.
knownFalsePositives: Some consoles show metadata on the span rather than the trace row; set it on both so the filter works either way.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites

A Splunk Agent Observability project for the application and one Agent Stream per environment or agent inside it. Do not create a second project for the same application: a second project splits the traces. The agent reads `SPLUNK_AO_PROJECT` and `SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM` from the environment. SaaS tenants authenticate with `SPLUNK_AO_REALM` and `SPLUNK_AO_O11Y_TOKEN`; on-prem tenants with `SPLUNK_AO_API_KEY` plus `SPLUNK_AO_CONSOLE_URL`. Install the SDK with `pip install splunk-ao` (`pip install "splunk-ao[langchain]"` for the LangChain callback).

Step 1 — Instrument the agent

Set tags and metadata on `start_trace` and on the spans; `conclude()` has no metadata argument. Keys and values are strings, 256 characters, flat. Trace-level metadata did not appear on the trace record in field testing; span metadata did.

Step 2 — Configure in Splunk Agent Observability

In the trace table, add `consumer` as a column and filter on it.

Step 3 — Validate

Send requests as two test consumers and confirm the filter separates them. This use case was written from the Splunk Agent Observability documentation without access to a tenant, so it ships as a draft. Confirm each step in the Splunk Agent Observability console before promoting it.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Share a monthly spend-by-consumer view with the agent's budget owner.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

Filter returns nothing: the key is only on the trace; add it to the agent spans too. In read-back results metadata is the JSON string `user_metadata_splunk_ao.metadata`.
grandmaExplanation: We label each question with who asked it, so we can see who uses the assistant most and what that costs.

productArtifacts.body:
meta = {"consumer": team_or_user_id}  # internal id, not raw PII; flat strings up to 256 characters
logger.start_trace(input=user_text, name="request", metadata=meta)
logger.add_agent_span(input=user_text, name="answer", metadata=meta)
